content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Courses teachable

Renting platforms like Teachable or Gumroad offer convenience but zero sovereignty. They host your content, process payments, and handle delivery — until they don't. Stripe's country restrictions and PayPal's arbitrary freezes prove this. Owning your stack means GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for logic, Supabase for storage, and NOWPayments for crypto payments. You control every layer. No platform can shut you down or change the rules mid-game. The tradeoff? You handle deployment. The reward? Permanent infrastructure.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms exclude countries based on compliance costs, not creator value. Stripe's 46-country limit isn't expanding fast enough for creators in Zimbabwe, Venezuela, or Ethiopia. PayPal's 180-day fund holds are a death sentence for cashflow. Sovereign stacks bypass this entirely. Crypto payments via NOWPayments work in every country. No KYC. No buyer accounts needed. BSC, Solana, or TRON networks keep fees under $0.10 per transaction. The platform's country list becomes irrelevant when you own the pipes.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Teachable takes 5% plus Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30. Gumroad takes 8.5% plus payment fees. PayPal holds funds for months in restricted regions. Sovereign stacks cut the middlemen. NOWPayments charges 0.5% for crypto processing. Cloudflare Workers and Pages are free. Supabase's free tier handles thousands of orders. Your only real cost is deployment time or a one-time stack fee. Payments hit your wallet the moment they confirm on-chain. No platform skimming. No delayed payouts.
Platforms exclude countries. Sovereign stacks exclude nobody.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Platforms own your customer data, your content, and your revenue stream. They can change terms overnight. Sovereign stacks give you full data ownership. Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive delivers files instantly post-payment. Automation runs on your rules, not theirs. Once deployed, COREMERCH has no access. No subscriptions. No platform lock-in. You own the code, the data, and the process. This is infrastructure sovereignty — not renting, but owning.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you need a course live in 48 hours without technical debt, the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments — fully configured and tested. If you prefer DIY, the Sovereign Blueprint ($47) provides docs and code. Renting platforms make sense only if your country is on their list and you trust their terms forever. For everyone else, owning your stack is the only permanent solution. Choose architecture over workarounds.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

If Stripe is unavailable in your country, deploy a sovereign commerce stack using GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for crypto payments. This bypasses platform restrictions entirely. Payments process on-chain with 0.5% fees, and you own every component. No country lists. No fund holds. Permanent infrastructure.
Crypto payments cost 0.5%. Platforms take 5-8.5% plus fees.

Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
